title: Island Demonstration
summary: Seeded Perlin island generation with a full save and load system.
description:
Players start in a menu with no character loaded. They can create a new world, which picks a random seed and generates a 250x250 island out of 5x5 blocks, or load one they saved earlier.

Terrain height comes from layered Perlin noise multiplied by a radial falloff, so the island sinks below sea level at the edges. Block type is chosen by height: sand near the water, then grass, stone and snow, with dirt filling the layers underneath.

Every block is serialized as type and grid position, then written to a DataStore on player leave and on BindToClose. DataStore calls retry with exponential backoff, saves are versioned for future schema migrations, and a busy flag stops a second world loading on top of the first.
